subsystems.name: Ancilla (clock) register
subsystems.role: holds the phase as a binary fraction; each extra qubit buys one more bit of precision.

subsystems.name: Controlled-unitary oracle
subsystems.role: applies the unitary U, raised to powers of two, conditioned on the ancilla.
parts: arithmetic for modular exponentiation, or Trotterised time evolution

subsystems.name: Inverse quantum Fourier transform
subsystems.role: converts accumulated phases into a readable binary number.
parts: swap network, or truncated approximate version

subsystems.name: Target register and state preparation
subsystems.role: the eigenvector whose eigenvalue is being extracted.

subsystems.name: Fault-tolerant execution layer
subsystems.role: makes a deep circuit survive noise long enough to finish.
parts: logical qubits in an error-correcting code

subsystems.name: Readout and classical post-processing
subsystems.role: turns measured bits into a useful answer.

buildSteps.title: Choose the unitary and the question
buildSteps.detail: Decide what operator U represents — modular multiplication for factoring, or a molecular Hamiltonian — and which eigenvalue you want from it.

buildSteps.title: Compile the operator into gates
buildSteps.detail: Encode U as elementary gates, for example a modular-exponentiation circuit, or a sequence of short time-evolution steps for a Hamiltonian.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the target register
buildSteps.detail: For simulation, prepare a good approximation to the ground state; for factoring, initialise the work register to 1 and put the rest in superposition.

buildSteps.title: Create the ancilla superposition
buildSteps.detail: Hadamard gates on m ancilla qubits put them in an equal superposition of all 2^m values, setting the achievable precision to roughly 2^-m.

buildSteps.title: Apply the controlled-unitary ladder
buildSteps.detail: Apply U, U², U⁴ … U^(2^(m-1)), each conditioned on one ancilla qubit. This ladder is the bulk of the circuit depth and the dominant cost.

buildSteps.title: Invert the quantum Fourier transform
buildSteps.detail: Rotate the ancilla register so the accumulated phase becomes a binary fraction. Approximate it by dropping the smallest rotations, or use an iterative single-ancilla variant with classical feedback.

buildSteps.title: Measure and post-process
buildSteps.detail: Read the ancilla in the computational basis and repeat. Continued fractions recover the answer in factoring; averaging gives an energy estimate in simulation.

buildSteps.title: Run fault-tolerantly
buildSteps.detail: Encode everything into logical qubits, distil the magic states needed for the non-Clifford rotations, execute under a decoder, and tune the precision against the depth you can afford.

prerequisites.why: the circuit is far too deep for physical qubits; experiments have shown logical qubits outperforming their physical parts, but only a few at a time.
every gate error is multiplied by the circuit length, so even small per-gate faults overwhelm a long phase-estimation run.
determines how cheaply each controlled-U^(2^k) can be built, and therefore whether the algorithm is practical at all.
the rotations and arithmetic inside the controlled unitaries need non-Clifford gates that cost many noisy ancilla qubits each.
turns the measured phase bits into a factor on an ordinary computer — the easy half of Shor's algorithm, described in the mid-1990s.

pathway.milestone: phase estimation and its iterative single-ancilla variant run on a handful of noisy qubits, mostly to read out energies in small demonstrations
pathway.unlocks: proof that the primitive works end to end on real hardware.

pathway.milestone: enough logical qubits, each reliably better than its physical parts, to run a small fault-tolerant phase estimation
pathway.unlocks: chemistry and materials results beyond exact classical simulation.

pathway.milestone: resource-optimised variants using qubitisation and better block-encodings to cut depth and non-Clifford gate count
pathway.unlocks: the same precision on a much smaller machine.

pathway.milestone: cryptographically relevant factoring, with literature resource estimates running to millions of physical qubits
pathway.unlocks: the headline application of Shor's algorithm and the main reason to build machines at that scale.
